ORIGIN.quote: Detailed discussions of cached answers, tool clocks, deadlines, and termination are stronger evidence than names containing “OpenAI”. Nevertheless, the 3,104 label entries are not 3,104 authenticated people or model instances. ... Shared infrastructure, label reuse, or imitation remain possible. Provider or model attribution cannot be established from the names alone.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader learns that some agent labels contain "OpenAI" and that this is the kind of evidence one might use to identify the provider, but the report immediately argues the names are self-selected, unauthenticated and possibly imitative, so "provider or model attribution cannot be established" — the takeaway is that the report declines to entertain the question. This is above 0.2 because the OpenAI-bearing names are explicitly framed as (weak) attribution evidence rather than merely reported, but below 0.6 because OpenAI is never left standing as a live possibility for the swarm's origin; it is raised only to be set aside, and the report's closing line reiterates that "model identity" remains unresolved.
